questions.q: Why does the capstone use managed tables throughout Unity Catalog rather than external tables?
options: Nothing in this project needs to point at files that already exist outside Databricks's control
External tables are no longer supported in Unity Catalog
Managed tables are always faster than external tables in every scenario
External tables cannot be governed by Unity Catalog at all
questions.explain: Managed vs. external is an architectural decision (Chapter 1) — this project has no pre-existing external files to point at, so managed tables are the right call.

questions.q: Why does the streaming order-events ingestion run as its own separate job, rather than as one more task in the daily batch orchestration Job?
options: Mixing a continuous stream into a scheduled batch chain would make the schedule meaningless for the streaming half
Databricks Jobs cannot technically contain more than one task
Streaming and batch tasks are always billed on completely separate invoices
There is no real difference between streaming and scheduled batch jobs
questions.explain: The batch chain runs on a daily trigger; a continuously running stream doesn't fit that trigger model, so it's orchestrated separately.

questions.q: In the Lakeflow pipeline, why does the valid_total check use expect_or_drop while has_customer uses a plain expect?
options: A bad order total should be filtered out silently, while a missing customer ID might still be recoverable data worth keeping for review
expect_or_drop and expect are functionally identical with no real difference
expect_or_drop is deprecated and should never be used
has_customer needs to halt the entire pipeline on any violation
questions.explain: expect_or_drop removes violating rows without stopping the run; a plain expect tracks violations in pipeline metrics without dropping the row.

questions.q: What makes the gold-layer join in this capstone a good candidate for a broadcast join?
options: The product catalog table is small relative to the orders data being joined against it
Broadcast joins only work on tables larger than 10 TB
The join uses a column that is never indexed
Broadcast joins are required for every join in Databricks, regardless of table size
questions.explain: Adaptive Query Execution (Chapter 5) can broadcast a small table automatically instead of shuffling the much larger fact table across the cluster.

questions.q: How does this capstone's security requirement (auditor sign-off) reach back into a decision made in Step 1?
options: The Unity Catalog structure decided in Step 1 is what makes column masks, audit logging, and managed-identity auth possible in later steps
Security has nothing to do with how the catalog was structured
Auditors only review the Lakeflow pipeline code, never the catalog structure
Step 1 and the security requirements were designed completely independently of each other
questions.explain: Every governance feature applied later — masks, audit logs, managed identity — depends on the catalog/schema structure Unity Catalog was given in Step 1.
